(updated_at 2026-09-21). Todos os enums (triggersOn, triggersWhen, conditionType, operator,
propertyName, actionType, severity, status) são os da página. Nenhum workspace, nenhum deploy.
O que faz: quando um incidente nasce das regras 1 ou 2 (persistência como SYSTEM) e o host
é um servidor (nome começa por 'srv'), sobe a severidade para High, marca, passa a Active e
acrescenta as três tarefas de triagem que o Ciclo 3 provou serem as que decidem o caso.
IDs das regras: os GUIDs dos YAML em ../rules/. Em produção seriam os IDs de recurso das
regras criadas no workspace — o ARM do template não os conhece antes da criação (Dia 1: o ID
name: d9a4c2e7-3f18-4b6a-9e05-71c8f2a5d3b6

properties.displayName: Triage: SYSTEM persistence on servers -> High, tasks, Active

actionConfiguration.title: Confirm audit coverage before trusting silence
actionConfiguration.description: Check whether 'Audit Other Object Access Events' is enabled on the host. If it is NOT, absence of a matching 4698 alert means nothing (rule 2 is deaf, not clean). If it IS and only the 4688 rule fired, the task may have been created but not registered - verify with schtasks /query on the host.

actionConfiguration.title: Pull the full TaskContent XML and read Principal/Triggers/Actions
actionConfiguration.description: From SecurityEvent (EventID 4698, parse EventData) get TaskContent (~1.6 KB). Confirm <UserId>S-1-5-18</UserId>, the trigger (<Interval>, <BootTrigger>, <LogonTrigger>) and <Command>. RunLevel=LeastPrivilege does NOT mean low privilege when the principal is already SYSTEM (Ciclo 3.1).

actionConfiguration.title: Check for 4702 updates and \Microsoft\ evasion
actionConfiguration.description: Query EventID 4702 for the same TaskName in the last 24h (task edited after creation is out of rule 2 scope). List tasks registered under \Microsoft\ on this host created by non-Microsoft parents - the rules filter that path by design.
